sentences.text:
The petitioner in O.P.(MV) No. 189 of 2009 on the files of the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal,
Thalassery has preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal on account of the injuries sustained by him in a motor accident that occurred on 22.10.2008.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as follows:-
On 22.10.2008, at 5.30 p.m., while the petitioner was traveling in a bus bearing registration No.KL-14D/4798 from Kaithapram towards Kannur and when reached near Payyannur college bus stop, a lorry bearing registration No. KA-19-C-1469 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on the bus in which the petitioner was travelling.
Due to the impact of the hit, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The owner and driver of the offending lorry were arrayed as the 1st and 2nd respondents respectively, whereas the insurer of the said lorry was arrayed as the 3rd respondent.
4. The 3rd respondent contested the petition by filing written statement mainly disputing the quantum of compensation claimed.
However, the 3rd respondent admitted insurance coverage for the lorry involved in the accident.
During trial
, from 2025:KER:22060 the side of the petitioner Exts. A1 to A9 were marked.
The disability certificate issued from the hospital where the petitioner had undergone treatment was marked in evidence as Ext.X1.
No evidence, whatsoever, was adduced from the side of the respondent.

5. After trial, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing registration KA-19-C-1469 by the 2nd respondent, and being the insurer, the 3rd respondent was held liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation was quantified at Rs. 92,900/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation with proportionate costs.
Seeking enhancement of the said compensation awarded, the petitioner has come up with this appeal.

6. I heard Sri.M.V.Amaresan, the learned counsel appearing for petitioner, Smt.P.K.Santhama, the learned counsel for the respondent and also perused the impugned award as well as the available materials.
7. From the rival contentions raised, it is gatherable that the main dispute that revolves around this appeal is with respect to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

The 2025:KER:22060 learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is too meager and the Tribunal awarded such an amount as Manoj Kumar C.M vs The United India Insurance Company Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88829032/
2 compensation without considering the gravity and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident as well as the consequent hardships and inconveniences met by him.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar C.M vs The United India Insurance Company Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent would submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is reasonable, just, fair, and, adequate and hence, warrants no interference.
8. A perusal of the impugned award indicates that there is some merit in the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner regarding the inadequacy of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
For the purpose of determining the compensation under the head of permanent disability and loss of earnings, the Tribunal assessed the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs. 4,500/-.
It is true that no convincing evidence, whatsoever, was produced from the side of the petitioner to prove his actual occupation and income.
Nonetheless, the accident occurred in the year 2008.

Therefore,
in view of the principles laid down in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance 2025:KER:22060 Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the Tribunal ought to have assessed the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.6,500/-.
9.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance 2025:KER:22060 Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner was aged 38 years at the time of the accident.
Therefore, in view of the decision in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010 (2) KLT 802 (SC)], the multiplier to be reckoned is 15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010 (2) KLT 802 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove that the petitioner suffered permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident, a disability certificate issued from the hospital where the petitioner underwent treatment is seen produced in evidence and marked as Ext.X1.
A perusal of the disability certificate shows that the petitioner is affected with a whole-body disability of 1%.
In Ext. X1 certificate, it is made clear that, further assessment of disability can be made only after the removal of the implant.

However, the learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that there is no prospect of removing the implant in the near future as it will make the health condition of the petitioner more complicated and there is a chance of arousal of nerve issues.
Therefore, the only way out is to act upon the disability already assessed by the Tribunal.

Resultantly, the petitioner is entitled to get an amount of Rs. 11,700/- (Rupees 2025:KER:22060 Eleven Thousand Seven Hundred only) [Rs.
6,500/- x 12 x 15 x 1/100] as compensation under the head of permanent disability.
10. Consequent to the revision in the monthly income, corresponding enhancement must be made to the compensation awarded under the head of loss of earnings also.
For the purpose of determining compensation under the said head, the Tribunal loss of earnings for a period of two months only.

The petitioner had sustained the following injuries in the accident;
Fracture mid shaft humerus with butterfly fragment and radial nerve palsy right
Considering the nature of the injuries sustined by the petitioner, I am of the view that, he would have been prevented from doing any work or earning any income at least for a period of six months.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to get an amount of Rs. 39,000/- (Rs. 6,500/- x 6) under the head of loss of earnings.

After deducting the already awarded amount of Rs.9,000/- under the said head, the petitioner is entitled to get an amount of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) as additional compensation under the head of loss of earnings.
11. A perusal of the impugned award further reveals that the Tribunal awarded only a nominal amount of Rs. 20,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.

It is apparent that the Manoj Kumar C.M vs The United India Insurance Company Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88829032/
3 2025:KER:22060 petitioner had sustained several injuries including fracture in the accident.

entities.text: Manoj Kumar C.M vs The United India Insurance Company Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, he had undergone eleven days of inpatient treatment in connection with the accident.

Considering the nature of the injuries and the treatment procedures underwent by him, I am of the view that the pain and sufferings endured by the petitioner ought not have been overlooked by the Tribunal while awarding compensation under the head of pain and sufferings.

I am of the view that an amount of Rs. 35,000/- has to be awarded under the head of pain and sufferings, entitling the petitioner to get an additional compensation of Rs. 15,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.

12. Similarly, under the head of loss of amenities and enjoyment in life, only a meager amount of Rs.
10,000/- is seen awarded by the Tribunal.

Considering the inconveniences and hardships endured by the petitioner in connection with the accident, I am of the view that an amount of Rs. 20,000/-
has to be awarded under the head of pain and sufferings, entitling the petitioner to get an additional compensation of Rs. 10,000/- under the head of loss of amenities and enjoyment in life.
13. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads appears to be reasonable and justifiable and hence, 2025:KER:22060 no interference is warranted.

Hence, an amount of Rs.
66,700/- (Rs. 11,700/- + Rs. 30,000/- + Rs. 15,000/- + Rs. 10,000/-) has to be added towards the total compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

In the light of the aforesaid observations and findings, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of Rs. 66,700/- (Rupees Sixty Six Thousand Seven Hundred only) with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit, after deducting interest for a period of 1128 days, i.e., the period of delay in preferring this appeal and as directed by this Court on 22.08.2019 in C.M. Appln.
No.2588/2018.

The respondent insurance company is ordered to deposit the enhanced compensation with interest before the Tribunal with proportionate costs within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.
